All done. The implementation compiles, passes correctness (5/5 trials), and runs at ~10 μs (mean) on MI300X.

Here's what's in [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level2_moonbridge_no_examples/p33/round1/output_model_new.py):

**Two AveLang kernels:**

- **`gemm_scale_kernel`** — Tiled GEMM (BM=64, BN=64, BK=64) using shared memory with BF16 inputs, FP32 accumulation, and fused bias+scale epilogue. 16×16 threads per block, each computing a 4×4 sub-tile. Outputs BF16.

- **`batchnorm_eval_kernel`** — Element-wise eval-mode BatchNorm using `running_mean`/`running_var` (not batch statistics). One thread per element, 256 threads per block.

The key fix was recognizing the eval harness runs in **eval mode**, so BatchNorm must use the stored running statistics rather than computing batch moments. That's also why the BN kernel is a simple element-wise op — no reduction needed.
